proposals.relationship: Noiriel credits Marx with prompting his philosophical self-education and later retains dialectical analysis while rejecting reductive class formulas.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 first answer recalls evening philosophy courses to understand Capital, followed by disenchantment rather than permanent doctrinal allegiance. Own 2019 dialectic answer explicitly says this approach reconciled him with Marx while adding sociological understanding of state and culture. No full Marx original newly read; his empirical reconstruction and mixed intellectual resources remain distinct.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, first answer, J’avais vécu cela en tant qu’étudiant

proposals.relationship: Noiriel acknowledges Althusser’s injunction to learn theoretical thinking as an exercise that later helped him challenge philosophical pretension.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 first answer says he retained intellectual gymnastics after Marxist disenchantment and used them against pseudo-treatises of historical epistemology. This is a bounded methodological resource, not endorsement of all Althusser’s philosophy or proof of direct personal teaching. No exact original Althusser work is identified or read.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, first answer, Néanmoins, comme j’avais tenté

proposals.relationship: Noiriel names reading Foucault among the formative philosophical work through which he learned to defend his historical research practice.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 formation account says an initially alienating theory course incited intensive reading of Lévi-Strauss, Althusser, Foucault, Deleuze and Lacan, through which he gradually forged intellectual tools. Foucault is one of several credited authors, not a sole teacher or wholesale allegiance. No specific title, direct supervision or original body reading is invented; the broader collective reading is retained explicitly.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, first answer, Et c’est en me plongeant

proposals.relationship: Noiriel explicitly credits Elias’s work as an important resource in developing his sociohistorical research.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2019 socio-historian answer says he relied extensively on Elias and regards him as one of the founders of socio-history. This is Noiriel’s retrospective acknowledgment and terminology, not an atlas claim that one scholar founded the whole field. It coexists with Noiriel’s more restrictive 2006 distinction reported by Hamman; neither complete original book is newly read.
primary_locators: CNRS2019, Vous vous définissez socio-historien, derived paragraph12

proposals.relationship: Noiriel uses Weber to distinguish practical historical inquiry from foundational epistemology and to analyze power relations as capable of solidarity as well as domination.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 answers invoke Weber’s anatomy/walking analogy and the practical language needed to defend research, explicitly unable to recall the exact latter text. Own 2019 explains his relational conception with Weber and uses legitimate violence in discussing state formation. These are attributed conceptual uses, not exact Weber quotations independently authenticated or acceptance of every historical generalization.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, epistemology definition and Rorty answers
CNRS2019, popular-history and state answers, derived12–13

proposals.relationship: Noiriel criticizes Veyne’s historical epistemology for addressing professional historians in language he regards as accessible mainly to philosophers.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 first answer specifies Comment on écrit l’histoire and objects to the gap between the professed historian audience and philosophical language. The criticism concerns practical disciplinary usefulness and asymmetries of authority, not a rejection of every Veyne argument. He also acknowledges the broader reflexive evolution associated with Veyne and de Certeau. Veyne’s book and replies are not newly read.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, first answer, Pour dire les choses autrement; note identifying Seuil1971

proposals.relationship: Noiriel criticizes Furet’s denunciation of positivism for blurring the authority of journalistic intervention and scholarly historical research.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 Bouveresse answer names Furet and argues that attacks on positivism could undermine research autonomy by putting a Nouvel Observateur article on the same plane as a scholarly article. This is Noiriel’s retrospective critical judgment, with his own allowance for multiple legitimate activities when clearly characterized. No particular Furet article, original exchange or reply newly read; no blanket assessment of Furet’s scholarship.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, Bouveresse answer, J’ai vu comment des historiens-journalistes

proposals.relationship: Noiriel opposes the position he attributes to Latour that social science is only a form of literature, using Bouveresse’s defense of science as a resource.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 Bouveresse answer explicitly names Latour in this attributed objection. The resource is mediated through Bouveresse, whose role is retained and whose endpoint is absent. The linked note gives the Sokal/Bouveresse controversy but neither Latour’s original text nor a reply is newly read; this edge records Noiriel’s criticism rather than independently adjudicating Latour’s position.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, Bouveresse answer, D’une manière plus globale; associated Sokal/Bouveresse note

proposals.relationship: Noiriel disputes Chartier’s characterization of his work as hostile to philosophy, distinguishing pragmatism from foundational philosophy.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2012 Rorty answer calls Chartier’s review otherwise very positive before rejecting this particular characterization. He names Wittgenstein, Rorty and Bouveresse as philosophical resources and rejects only the proposed monopoly of foundationalism. Note identifies Chartier, Entre Clovis et Lavisse: de nouveaux espaces à créer, Le Monde 4 October 1996. That original review remains unread, so no fresh reverse criticism or claim that it contained only this objection.
primary_locators: Ortiz2012 part1, Rorty answer, Contrairement à ce qu’écrivait Roger Chartier; associated Chartier note

proposals.relationship: Hamman reports Noiriel’s methodological reservation that Elias’s limited direct archival and field inquiry places his work closer to historical sociology than to Noiriel’s narrower socio-history.
proposals.evidence_note: Hamman 2006 paragraph10 quotes Noiriel35 claiming Elias never personally undertook archival or field research, then cautions readers against interpreting the distinction as a general incapacity of sociologists to conduct empirical work. This is a named reader’s presentation of Noiriel’s restrictive classification, not an independently verified account of Elias’s research practice. Hamman’s own caution, his strong overall praise and Noiriel’s later explicit Elias debt remain; original2006book/Elias originals unread.
primary_locators: Hamman2006, numbered paragraph10, final discussion of Noiriel35
